function: Learned group-level allocation of bandwidth, transmit power and computing resources among user groups in an ISAC network to maximize QoE under sensing CRB constraints (p. 8).
system: Two BSs with 32 transmit and receive antennas, 30 mobile users, downlink ISAC waveforms, no RIS, 28 GHz (n257) and 39 GHz (n260), 400 MHz bandwidth (p. 11).
method: Taylor TD deep reinforcement learning (fully connected 256x128x64 network, 240 training episodes) chooses group-level allocation; SCA convex optimization (not learned) handles user level (pp. 8-9, 11-12).
data_channel: Custom simulation: path loss 32.4+20log(d)+20log(fc) dB, radar-equation sensing gain, real Waterloo layout; YouTube-8M videos and swipe data; no 3GPP or measured channel (p. 11).
test_conditions: Trained 240 episodes of 60 steps; evaluated by sweeping users (22-30), bandwidth, computing resources and CRB thresholds; no stated transfer to unseen conditions (pp. 11-14).
baselines: Non-learned: w/o DA (round robin), Heuristic (greedy). Learned: PDRL (five-layer BDQN) and HDRL (TD3 with hierarchical reward) (p. 12).
metrics: Average user QoE (MOS-based), reward convergence, QoE cumulative distribution, QoE gain in percent versus baselines (pp. 12-14).
complexity: Order O(E·N·(2V^3 + L_policy + log|D|)) for the full algorithm: interior-point convex solves, network inference, replay sampling (p. 11).
openness: none; uses public YouTube-8M and short-video swipe datasets (links p. 11), no code released, supplementary material holds the Theorem 1 proof (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 11: "calculated based on the standard radar equation" for sensing, and a 32.4 + 20 log(d) + 20 log(fc) dB path loss for communication: a custom simulator, with no 3GPP TR 38.901 model and no measured channel; the real-world data are videos and swipe traces.
q2_support: p. 13: "compared across different numbers of users" with bandwidth and computing fixed: parameter sweeps; the paper never says a model trained under one setting is tested on another or whether it is retrained per setting (training on p. 11).
q3_support: p. 12: "a five-layer branch dueling Q network (BDQN) [47]" and HDRL [48] (TD3) are the learned baselines; round robin (w/o DA) and the greedy heuristic are non-learned; all are compared on QoE (p. 13, Fig. 8).
q4_support: p. 11: "O(E · N · (2 V 3 + Lpolicy + log |D|))" is the stated total computational complexity of the proposed algorithm (V decision variables, Lpolicy network operations).
q5_support: p. 11: "YouTube 8M dataset: https://research.google.com/youtube8m/index.html" and the swipe dataset are public data of the learning task, not channels or signals; no code or channel data is released (supplement holds the Theorem 1 proof, p. 9).
notes: Borderline above_phy: the objective is video QoE and the learned action also includes computing resources (above PHY), but bandwidth and transmit power are learned jointly with it under sensing CRB constraints, so kept as area 5. The DA module (ARIMA, distance correlation, curve fitting) is not the learned PHY function. Reviewer to confirm.
